android.desc:
Have a map with more details then online maps? Make a photo of it, calibrate* it (using openstreetmaps.org within the app), and use the location of your phone to navigate the map.
Works great with local travel maps, but can be combined with (drawn) maps like pirate maps as well.
(*Calibrating is unnecessary if you received the photo from someone who already calibrated it within the app, and shares it from the app.)

App uses service to receive locations while the app is not visible. In this way the app can animate from where you started the walk. Swipe the app away to stop the service; the app will save any maps you have already matched against a background (but you will lose your location history). 
Watch the video to see the app in action.

Want to test new features? Features such as drawing on the map was first available in the open test version before it landed in the 'production' version.
(To participate: visit https://play.google.com/apps/testing/nl.vanderplank.navigateanymap ).
Latest feature in open test: Experimental version of exporting the map (pre-matched), the track, or both. If the last option is choosen, you can view and show the track you walked on the following website:
https://vanderplank.nl/navigateanymap/view_my_trails/
You will need to upload the exported map and trail (do not worry: these will not leave your device, but are used locally by your browser) and thus showcast your trail.

quotes.text:
I created several. The most recent: an Android app that lets you navigate any map, e.g. the one you just make a picture of: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=nl.vanderplank.navigateanymap

I use this one myself: we like to take walks, and not always are the routes marked that clearly. Still only a handful of users, but usefull I guess for anyone that wished that e.g. Google maps made it possible to upload a picture to be laid upon the background map.

Earlier apps:
1 - the UNofficial Prezi Player app. Used in 56 countries, it relied upon a hack to be able to play a prezi on an Android phone or tablet. Was quite succesfull, untill of course Prezi made an official Android app of their own. (Actually: demonstrated it to Prezi and they asked nicely to make sure no one would think it was official)

2 - a ‘fixer’ of Prezi’s. This was in the time that Prezi’s could become ‘corrupt’ as one of the elements was to small such that the code would give a ‘divided by zero’ problem. I fixed a lot of these errors by hand, before I made a (paid) service, and before that a java program that fixed this by going into an XML file, finding the smallest item, and enlarging it.
(Am very happy with Prezi by the way, was invited (but declined in the end) to join them for a hackathon in Budapest, was made their first ‘prezi champion of the month’, and they gifted me a life long licence for their software).
